options.how: Seasons of about three months each bring a new Battle Pass, map changes and themed content, with mid-season updates in between.
Shipped as a complete game; the major later addition was one large paid expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree.

sources.note: Fortnite: seasonal Battle Pass and updates
Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree expansion

options.how: A complete story at launch, followed by two story expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, then no new content.
Free to play with a steady stream of patches, new frames and story updates, so the game keeps changing years after launch.

sources.note: The Witcher 3: Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine expansions
Warframe: free to play with ongoing patch notes and new content

options.how: A single-player card game with a fixed story and an end; you buy it once and the content you get is the content there is.
Monthly themed seasons, new cards and frequent balance patches keep the card pool and meta moving.

sources.note: Inscryption: single-player, Daniel Mullins Games, 2021
Marvel Snap: new seasons, balance updates and patch notes

options.how: Bought once, then grown through three paid expansions (Ashes of Malmouth, Forgotten Gods, Fangs of Asterkarn) and free updates.
Free to play; frequent challenge leagues run as separate game worlds with their own ladders, economies and rule changes.

sources.note: Grim Dawn: expansions Ashes of Malmouth, Forgotten Gods and Fangs of Asterkarn
Grim Dawn: one-time purchase on Steam
Path of Exile: free to play; race leagues run frequently as separate worlds with their own ladders and economies

options.how: Shipped complete on disc with its full event list and cars; no seasons or content drops.
Over 40 content updates added cars, races and features, with a rotating Festival Playlist of seasonal events.

sources.note: Burnout 3: Takedown: complete boxed release
Forza Horizon 5: over 40 content updates, Festival Playlist

options.how: A cartridge with 120 Power Stars and nothing more to download; the design had to be complete on day one.
A subscription world that has kept adding expansions for decades, dozens so far, with new zones and level caps.

sources.note: Super Mario 64: 120 Power Stars
EverQuest: dozens of expansions

options.how: The official Creation Kit edits the same plugin files the game uses; mods can add quests, items and scripts and share via Workshop.
No mod support; the Vanguard anti-cheat runs at kernel level from boot to block third-party software.
The game is a platform: players build experiences in Roblox Studio and publish them for others, with creator payouts.

sources.note: Skyrim: Creation Kit and plugins
Valorant: Vanguard anti-cheat
Roblox: Studio and user-created experiences

options.how: Community mappers make and submit the beatmaps; a ranking procedure (or loved status) decides which get leaderboards.
A curated list of 385 Final Fantasy tracks charted by the developer; new songs arrive only as paid DLC packs, with no chart editor.

sources.note: osu!: mappers submit beatmaps; ranking procedure or loved status grants leaderboards
Theatrhythm Final Bar Line: 385 selected tracks, songs added through DLC packs

options.how: The bundled World Editor can change almost every aspect of the game, so players built custom maps and campaigns.
Riot staff design every champion and map; custom games only set lobby options such as team size and bots, not new content.

sources.note: Warcraft III: World Editor manipulates almost every aspect of the game for custom maps and campaigns
League of Legends: Riot staff create champions; custom games are private lobbies with set properties

options.how: Levels and assets live in WAD files; players load PWADs on top of the base game, so fan maps spread freely.
Blizzard designs every card and set; collections live on its servers, so players cannot add content.

sources.note: Doom: IWAD and PWAD files
Hearthstone: Blizzard-released card sets

options.how: Create mode ships the same tools the levels were built with; players publish levels online for others to play.
Every level is hand-built by the developer, with daily and weekly online challenges instead of user content.

sources.note: LittleBigPlanet: create and share levels
Rayman Legends: developer-built levels and challenges

options.how: Valve released an SDK; total conversions like Counter-Strike and Team Fortress Classic began as Half-Life mods.
No mod tools; servers and content are run by the publisher and anti-cheat bans altered clients.

sources.note: Half-Life: SDK and mods
Call of Duty: Warzone: publisher-run service

options.how: Every pixel is simulated in a world that is different every run, with permadeath, so replays differ in how fire, liquid and spells collide.
Any monster can be spared or killed; those choices lead to different authored scenes, boss friendships and endings on later runs.

sources.note: Noita: a unique world every time you play, permanent death, every pixel simulated
Undertale: you don't have to kill anyone, each enemy can be defeated nonviolently, multiple endings

options.how: Each new world is generated with its own history and legends, then simulated dwarves, creatures and populations produce unwritten stories.
Thousands of choices branch an authored story into dozens of endings; replays reveal scenes and outcomes you missed.

sources.note: Dwarf Fortress: world generation, Legends mode history and procedural creatures (developer notes)
Detroit: Become Human: thousands of choices and dozens of possible endings, no playthrough the same

options.how: Random dungeons and permanent death; replay comes from item, monster and terrain interactions, not new content.
New Game+ and over a dozen endings reward replays with authored scenes based on when you face the final boss.

sources.note: NetHack: 1987 release, permanent death
Chrono Trigger: multiple endings

options.how: You play a dynasty through successive heirs; traits, claims and plots between AI characters create each campaign's story.
Origin characters, classes and branching quest choices unlock different authored scenes, companions and endings.

sources.note: Crusader Kings II: dynasty play through heirs
Baldur's Gate 3: origins and branching choices

options.how: A-Type is an endless marathon: the same seven pieces and one rule set produce a different board every game.
Replay grows with the song library: each music pack adds authored tracks and charts to master.

sources.note: Tetris (Game Boy): A-Type endless marathon
Beat Saber: music packs

options.how: Simple and advanced track editors with 3000+ blocks; the best player-made tracks rotate into weekly and Arcade channel play.
Every course is built by Nintendo; new tracks arrived only as paid Booster Course Pass waves, with no course editor.

sources.note: Trackmania: simple and advanced track editors, best player-created tracks featured weekly and in the Arcade channel
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: Booster Course Pass DLC waves 1 to 4, no course editor listed

options.how: Random shop Jokers from a pool of 150 stack scoring effects with each other and your deck, so every run builds a different engine.
Seven origin characters each bring a written backstory, dedicated dialogue and a personal quest, so replays unlock new authored story.

sources.note: Balatro: 150 Jokers, random shop generation and synergy with other Jokers and deck composition
Baldur's Gate 3: seven origins with predefined backstory, unique interactions and a personal quest
